gap: No result ChatGPT got states a timed face-recognition run on candidate hardware. Mighty Gadget (James Smythe) timed a 220,000-photo library at about 12 hours on the Intel UGREEN DXP4800 Plus and about 36 hours on the ARM DH4300 Plus.
standout_why: I opened the two cited rival comparison pages, homelabcompass.com/compare/immich-vs-synology-photos and esp32.co.uk/synology-photos-vs-immich-vs-photoprism. Neither has any measured figure. HomeLabCompass only says Immich 'moves much faster' and Synology is 'steady'. Esp32 says it is 'a documentation-based comparison, not a claim that we benchmarked'. Its 25 W number is an 'example assumption'. The Synology KB and spec pages ChatGPT cited list features and RAM rules, not timings or watts. I did not open itechguides, androidcentral, supinfo or whoismcafee, which ranked but were not cited. Our current page has no measured figures at all.
decides: This confirms that x86 boxes are worth it over UGREEN's cheaper ARM DH models for a family library: Mighty Gadget's face-recognition pass took 3× as long on the DH4300 Plus. It also backs pairing Immich with the 8 GB DXP2800 rather than a stock 2 GB Synology DS225+/DS425+. ComputingForGeeks measured Immich using about 2.4–2.6 GiB of RAM, which is more than those Synologys ship with, so a RAM upgrade comes first there. The power figures don't change the pick, but they let the page state running cost per box with a name attached.

findings.label: Face-recognition processing time, 220,000-photo library (UGOS Photos)
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus Review - A Powerful 10GbE NAS That Challenges the Market Leaders (Mighty Gadget, James Smythe)
findings.note: Quote: 'On the DXP4800 Plus, similar processing completed in roughly 12 hours.' Published 2025-11-14, updated 2026-04-01. My arithmetic: about 18,300 photos/hour. If that rate holds, a 50,000-photo family library takes about 2.7 h. That is a linear extrapolation, not a measurement.

findings.label: Face-recognition processing time, 220,000-photo library (UGOS Photos)
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus Review (Mighty Gadget, James Smythe)
findings.note: Quote: 'Processing 220,000 photos for face recognition took about 36 hours on the DH4300 Plus.' Same reviewer and same library as the DXP4800 Plus figure. That is 3× longer, about 6,100 photos/hour. The DH2300 uses the same Rockchip ARM platform, but it was not tested.

findings.label: Measured power draw
findings.value: 39–45 W during photo transfers; 64 W peak; 32 W in the evening
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800 Plus Review (Mighty Gadget, James Smythe)
findings.note: The drive population isn't stated. The same reviewer measured the DH4300 Plus at about 21–22 W for similar workloads.

findings.label: Measured power draw at the wall
findings.value: 0.6 W off with WoL; 5.6 W standby; 14.5 W during data transfer
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test – Kann die kleine Variante überzeugen? (igor'sLAB, Tim Kutzner)
findings.note: Measured with only one NVMe SSD installed and the HDDs removed, so two spinning drives would add to this. Published 2024-05-08, modified 2025-05-31.

findings.note: Posted 2025-08-25. The same page also gives 28.25 W access and 6.10 W hibernation, but those match Synology's rated spec, so treat them as the maker's figures rather than measurements. Distance and method for the dB readings are not stated.

findings.label: Noise (NASCompares)
findings.source_title: Synology DS225+ NAS Review – Should You Buy? (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews)
findings.note: Posted 2025-08-04. Distance and method are not stated, so it can't be compared with igor'sLAB's 40 cm readings. The page's 16.98 W / 6.08 W power figures match Synology's spec and are not independent measurements.

findings.label: Immich RAM footprint and ML throughput (lab-timed, CPU-only)
findings.value: 2,430 MiB idle with photos loaded; 2,620 MiB peak during face detection; face detection 3.95 photos/s, CLIP smart search 12.7 photos/s, OCR 3.1 photos/s
findings.source_title: Best NAS for Immich and Photo Backup (2026) (ComputingForGeeks, Eugene Otieno)
findings.note: Immich v3.3.3 on a 4-vCPU Core i7-6700 Proxmox VM with 8 GB RAM. 497 NASA photos. Tested 2026-10-20. Not run on any candidate NAS. The ~2.4–2.6 GiB footprint is more than the stock 2 GB in the DS225+ and DS425+, and fits within the DXP2800's 8 GB. Raising face-detection concurrency to 4 made it 9% slower.

unsourced: A timed Synology Photos face or object recognition run on a J4125 box (DS225+, DS425+, DS224+). I searched reviewer and forum results and found only untimed forum reports and a blog estimate with no method.
